Overview

Linux swap memory is disk space used when physical RAM (Random Access Memory) is fully utilized. It acts as an overflow area for RAM, allowing the operating system to continue functioning even when available physical memory is insufficient for all running applications and processes.

Swap space is a portion of a storage drive (e.g., SSD or HDD) reserved to extend the system’s memory capacity.

While slower than actual RAM due to disk I/O operations, it provides a fallback mechanism when RAM becomes overcommitted.

item.description:
Overview

Semantic Versioning (SemVer) is a versioning scheme that helps manage software versions meaningfully.

Rather than arbitrary number sequences, SemVer assigns meaning to version numbers, allowing both users and developers to easily understand the scope of changes.


SemVer Format

MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH

Components:

  • MAJOR: Incremented for incompatible API changes
  • MINOR: Incremented for backward-compatible new features
  • PATCH: Incremented for backward-compatible bug fixes

Understanding how external traffic reaches internal Pods in a Kubernetes cluster is essential for operations and troubleshooting. Incoming requests don’t simply connect directly to Pods—they traverse multiple network components before reaching their final destination.

External traffic first enters the cluster through an Ingress Controller or LoadBalancer.
